overhead_model.form: 1/tg = (1/k_mem) * (1/ceiling) + t0 ; ordinary least squares on fit points
overhead_model.caveat: Only the CUDA fit is well conditioned (22 points, ceilings 99-934 t/s). Metal gives a negative t0 because its high-ceiling points are Apple Ultra chips while the low-ceiling ones are older M1/M4 Max builds; Vulkan-ROCm mixes three vendors' drivers; CPU ceilings span 10-28 t/s only, so t0 is not identifiable there. Treat these as descriptive, not as calculator constants.

notes:
All measurement rows were fetched on 2026-09-15 from the cited GitHub pages (HTML flattened, or REST API markdown), the ggml-org bench files at commit 3795cc1e, one AMD ROCm blog page, and GGUF headers on Hugging Face (HTTP range requests). Each quote is the exact text line the number was read from; rows from rendered HTML tables have whitespace collapsed.
Formula (as requested): size_gb = size GiB x 1.073741824 (same convention as hardware.json dense calibration); bytes_active_gb_approx = size_gb x active_params / total_params, with total = llama-bench 'params' column and active = model card; ceiling_active = bandwidth / bytes_active; k_moe = tg / ceiling_active. ratio_vs_total_size = tg / (bandwidth / size_gb). KV cache and recurrent state are ignored (all tests are depth 0 except where flagged).
The approximation assumes every tensor is quantised at the file-average bit width. GGUF headers show that is wrong in model-specific ways: in gpt-oss MXFP4 files the non-expert tensors are Q8_0 (twice the bits of the experts), so the approximation UNDER-states bytes/token by ~19% (20b) and ~23% (120b) and k_moe comes out low; in Qwen3/GLM Q4_K_M files the embedding (counted in the card's active params, but only gathered) makes it OVER-state by 4-7%. k_exact uses bytes read per decoded token computed from the GGUF tensor table (all non-expert tensors except token_embd, plus routed-expert tensors x used/total experts). If the calculator computes bytes as active_params x nominal bits/8 it reproduces the approximation, so k_moe (not k_exact) is the constant to pair with it.
Selection: single device, all layers on GPU (or CPU-only), no expert offload, no RPC/multi-GPU, default env. One point per (platform, backend, model file class) enters the fit; older builds of the same combination are kept with use_in_fit=false ('superseded') because llama.cpp MoE decode sped up a lot between Aug 2025 and Sep 2026 (RTX 5090 gpt-oss-20b: 282.5 -> 298.6 -> 359.7 t/s; M2 Ultra gpt-oss-20b 116.1 -> 130.0; M2 Ultra Qwen3-30B-A3B Q8_0 79.0 -> 94.4).
Caveats: several tests are tg32 (ggml-org bench files) or tg400 (issue #28196) rather than tg128; one is tg1024@d1024. CPU points are summary tables from fairydreaming (build 4663 + a local MoE warm-up patch) and ubergarm (Xeon, best thread count) with sizes inferred from the same quant type. The AMD blog point is Ollama, not llama-bench. Flash attention was on (-fa 1) in nearly all GPU rows. MLX/oMLX: no official MoE decode benchmark with a stated model size was found, so none is included.
No aggregator blogs or remembered numbers are used. Model active-parameter counts come from the model cards (URLs + quotes per point).
